ing: 14 oz canned palm nut cream (sauce graine)
whole, such as habanero, or to taste
st: Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for about 4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
In the same pot, cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, mashing them, until they break down into a sauce.
Return the chicken to the pot and add the palm butter, [[2 cups]] water, whole chili and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Stir well.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer for 45 minutes, stirring now and then.
The sauce should turn dark and thick and the oil will rise to the top. Chicken must reach 165°F (74°C) inside.
Remove the whole chili. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve hot with rice, fufu, or chikwangue.

ing: thawed; or collard greens or spinach
st: Soak the dried fish in hot water for 15 minutes, then flake it and remove any bones.
Put the cassava leaves and [[3 cups]] water in a large pot. Bring to a boil and cook for 30 minutes until tender.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] palm oil in a pan and cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the eggplant and cook for 5 minutes until starting to brown.
Stir the onion mixture, flaked fish, whole chili and [[1 tsp]] salt into the greens.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often. Add water if it gets dry.
The greens should be very soft and dark with oil showing on top.
Remove the whole chili and serve hot with fufu, rice or chikwangue.
Bring [[3 cups]] water to a boil in a heavy pot.
Mix the cassava flour and cornmeal with [[1 cup]] cold water in a bowl until no lumps remain.
Pour the paste into the boiling water slowly, stirring hard with a wooden spoon.
Cook over medium-low heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Keep turning and pressing the dough against the pot for 8 minutes more until it is smooth and stiff and pulls cleanly away from the sides.
While it cooks, wilt the spinach in a pan with [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 3 minutes.
Wet your hands or a bowl and shape the fufu into smooth balls.
Drizzle the balls with [[1 tbsp]] palm oil and serve hot with the spinach and a stew.

ing: whole tilapia or firm fish fillets
st: Rub the fish with the lemon juice, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Let sit 10 minutes.
Mix the onion, tomatoes, chili, garlic, [[2 tbsp]] oil and [[0.5 tsp]] salt in a bowl.
Warm the banana leaves briefly over a flame or in hot water to make them soft, then cut into 4 large squares.
Put a quarter of the fish on each leaf and cover with the vegetable mixture.
Fold the leaf over the fish to make a tight packet and tie with kitchen twine, or wrap in foil.
Steam on a rack over simmering water for 35 minutes, or grill over medium coals, turning once.
Check that the fish is opaque, flakes easily and reaches 145°F (63°C).
Open the packets carefully since steam will escape, and serve with chikwangue or rice.
Mix the cassava flour with [[2 cups]] warm water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a thick paste. Cover and ferment in a warm place for 12 hours, or skip for a milder loaf.
Cook the paste in a pot over medium heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for 10 minutes until it forms a smooth, thick dough.
Let it cool until you can handle it.
Soften the banana leaves over heat and cut into 4 large squares.
Shape the dough into 4 rolls. Wrap each tightly in leaves and tie with twine.
Bring [[10 cups]] water to a boil in a large pot. Lower in the bundles.
Boil gently for 90 minutes, turning once, until firm and the leaves have darkened.
Cool, unwrap and slice. Serve with [[1 tbsp]] palm oil and flaked smoked fish.
Soak the salt fish in cold water for 8 hours or overnight, changing the water 3 times, to remove the salt.
Drain and put the fish in a pot with fresh water to cover. Boil 15 minutes, then drain, remove skin and bones and break into chunks.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and whole chili. Cook for 10 minutes until saucy.
Add [[1 cup]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and bring to a simmer.
Stir in the fish and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes.
Taste the sauce for salt; it rarely needs more. Remove the whole chili.
Serve hot with fufu, rice or boiled plantains.

ing: boneless, cut into 1 inch cubes; or lamb
st: Mix the grated onion, chili, garlic, [[3 tbsp]] oil, lemon juice, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] pepper in a large bowl.
Add the goat meat and turn to coat. Marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Soak the skewers in water for 30 minutes so they do not burn.
Heat the grill or a grill pan to medium-high.
Thread the meat onto the skewers, leaving small gaps.
Grill for 12 to 15 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Goat should be tender; if still tough, cover and rest for 5 minutes.
Serve hot with onion slices, hot sauce, fried plantains or bread.
Slice each plantain on a slant into pieces about 0.5 inch thick.
Sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Heat [[0.5 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering.
Add plantains in a single layer, without crowding.
Fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden brown with crisp edges.
Lift out and drain on paper towels.
In the same skillet, cook the onion and chili for 2 minutes in a little of the leftover oil.
Serve the hot plantains topped with the onion and chili.
Stir the yeast and [[1 tbsp]] of the sugar into [[1 cup]] warm water. Wait 8 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, the remaining sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Add the yeast water and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Mix and knead for 8 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, until doubled.
Punch down the dough and pinch off pieces the size of a golf ball. Roll into smooth balls.
Cover and let rest for 15 minutes.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the dough balls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels. Serve warm.
Put the plantain chunks in a pot with [[6 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Cook for 25 minutes until very soft and a fork goes in easily.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] palm oil in a small pan and cook the onion (and chili if using) for 4 minutes.
Drain the plantains well and mash in a bowl until smooth and sticky.
Mix in the onion, ground peanuts and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Oil your hands lightly and shape the mash into 8 round balls.
Serve warm with stew, fish or greens.
